question: How do you build likelihoods and links for ordered categorical outcomes, zero-inflated counts and over-dispersed counts by combining simpler GLM components?
contributions: Ordered logit with cumulative link (Trolley data)
Continuous mixtures for over-dispersion: beta-binomial and gamma-Poisson

Do not use WAIC with beta-binomial or gamma-Poisson models unless sure; fall back on DIC.
results.quote: You should not use WAIC with these models, however, unless you are very sure of what you are doing.

results.claim: Half-Cauchy prior for theta is poorly efficient; an exponential prior samples better without changing inference.
results.quote: it is often the case that θ is poorly identified.

limits: Fits use quadratic approximation (map) or map2stan with rethinking 1st-edition syntax; WAIC is advised against for beta-binomial/gamma-Poisson.
Gamma-Poisson gets no worked example; over-dispersion is deferred to multilevel models (Ch. 12).
Trolley priors Normal(0,10) are safe only because of large data (9930 rows).
The ZIPoisson example is a simulation with one year of data (N=365) and intercept-only models.
practices: Validate a new hybrid model by simulating dummy data and recovering the data-generating process (p.331).
Transform the model to fit the measurement, not the measurement to fit the model (p.331).
Add predictors to ordered logit on the cumulative logit scale and subtract phi from each cutpoint so positive beta raises the mean response (p.338).
Start cutpoints in the right order; ordering matters, exact values do not (p.336).
Plot ordered-logit predictions as cumulative probability curves per response across a predictor, looping over posterior samples (p.340-341).
Put different predictors in the two linear models of a ZIPoisson as hypothesis dictates (p.344).
Compute likelihoods on the log scale (dzipois vs dzip) (p.346).
Use an exponential prior and a start value for beta-binomial theta; use constraints for positivity (p.348).
Prefer multilevel models over beta-binomial/gamma-Poisson for over-dispersion in practice (p.347).
Pass a list of models to ensemble if WAIC is not decisive (p.340).
For zero-inflated fishing counts use a Poisson offset from hours (11H6, p.353).

terms.definition: The cumulative probability of a value is the probability of that value or any smaller value; linking a linear model to it guarantees outcome ordering.
log Pr(y<=k)/(1-Pr(y<=k)) = alpha_k; the cumulative analog of the logit link.
A mixture model uses more than one simple probability distribution to model a mixture of causes; in effect more than one likelihood for the same outcome.
Observed variance exceeds that implied by the model's parameters after conditioning on all predictors, implying an omitted variable.
Each binomial count has its own probability of success drawn from a beta distribution with mean pbar and shape theta.
Each Poisson count has its own rate drawn from a gamma distribution with mean mu and scale theta.
Each count has its own independent continuous-distributed parameter; the likelihood averages over it: integral g(y|n,p) h(p|pbar,theta) dp.
